statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Section 99-19-71(1), read from the enrolled text of 2026 Miss. HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, provides that any person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor that is not a traffic violation, and who is a first offender, may petition the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the conviction was had for an order to expunge the conviction from all public records. Subsection (1) states no waiting period, no completion requirement and no pending-charge restriction; relief is permissive as to petitioning and is treated as discretionary. Under § 99-19-71(3) the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record of every expunction solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings, so an earlier expunction does not restore first-offender status. Section 99-19-72 levies a fee on each petition to expunge an offense under § 99-19-71, collected by the circuit clerk; whether it reaches a subsection (1) petition filed in justice or municipal court is recorded as unresolved.
doNotImport: Do not invent a waiting period, a sentence-completion requirement or a pending-charge bar; subsection (1) contains none.
Do not plead the subsection (2)(a) payment condition as a statutory element of this route; a zero balance is an advisable attachment only.
Do not certify first-offender status or the nontraffic classification; both are the participant's own initialled assertions, checked against the Mississippi criminal history record.
Do not handle a DUI, a traffic violation or a felony on this route; DUI and felonies have their own tracks.
Do not publish a fee amount; § 99-19-72's reach to justice and municipal courts is a recorded open question and the participant confirms the fee with the clerk.
Do not hardcode a court, county, cause number, prosecuting authority, the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties or the year 2020; every district-variable field is participant data.
Do not reuse the Fourth District models' indictment allegation, race field, five-year recital or attorney-signature phrasing.
Do not extend this family to another Mississippi pathway.

finalVerificationRequirements: Confirm from the certified judgment that the matter is a misdemeanor conviction, not a DUI, a traffic violation, a felony or a non-conviction disposition.

Copy the convicting court and its level, county or city, cause number, offence wording, code section, offence date, arrest date, arresting agency and conviction date from the court record and case papers, never from memory.
Obtain the Mississippi criminal history record from the Mississippi Criminal Information Center and initial the first-offender statement only if it shows no other conviction and no prior expungement.
Initial the nontraffic statement only if it is true; an uncertain classification is a reason to stop and get advice.

Confirm the fee amount, any pauper's-affidavit route, any local form preference and any approved-as-to-form practice with the records office of the convicting court before filing; no amount is published in this packet.

Confirm the prosecuting authority and its current mailing address with the court's records office, serve by United States mail or hand delivery, and complete the certificate only after service occurs.
The participant signs and dates the petition and certificate; the judge's entry and signing block and the prosecutor's approved-as-to-form block are never pre-filled.

filingDestination.statement: File the petition and proposed order with the clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the conviction was had. Call that court's records office first: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, municipal and justice courts are the least standardized courts in the state, and districts maintain their own petition and order preferences.
filingDestination.office: Clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court of conviction
filingDestination.sourceOfRule: MS.memo.json track ms-misd-1st, geography.venue, destination and rules.filing

feeAndWaiver.statement: No amount is published in this packet. Section 99-19-72 levies a fee on each petition to expunge an offense under § 99-19-71, collected by the circuit clerk, and this track is such a petition on the face of the statute; whether that fee reaches a subsection (1) petition filed in justice or municipal court is a recorded open question. The participant confirms the amount with the records office of the convicting court before filing.
feeAndWaiver.waiverStatement: A pauper's affidavit under general Mississippi practice, where the participant cannot pay; the participant asks the clerk which affidavit or waiver process that court accepts.
feeAndWaiver.sourceOfRule: MS.memo.json track ms-misd-1st, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver and the unresolved § 99-19-72 question

serviceAndNotice.statement: Deliver a true and correct copy of the petition and proposed order to the prosecuting authority for the court by United States mail or hand delivery, evidenced by the certificate of service: the district attorney for a circuit-district case, or the county or municipal prosecuting attorney for a lower court; in municipal court that is the city prosecutor, not the district attorney. No response or objection period is stated for subsection (1); the ten-day notice in subsection (2)(b) governs the felony track and is not imported.

postFilingTimeline.step: File the petition and proposed order with the clerk of the convicting court and pay the fee the clerk confirms, or file the pauper's affidavit that court accepts.
postFilingTimeline.timing: after every required-before-filing item is complete; subsection (1) states no waiting period

postFilingTimeline.step: Serve the prosecuting authority by United States mail or hand delivery and keep the completed certificate of service.
postFilingTimeline.timing: at or after filing, under the local mechanics confirmed with the clerk

postFilingTimeline.step: Some districts expect the prosecuting authority to approve the order as to form before the judge signs; the participant does not negotiate that step and the packet never pre-signs the block.
postFilingTimeline.timing: after service, at the court's or prosecutor's direction

postFilingTimeline.step: After the order issues, obtain certified copies and distribute them to every agency named in the order. Fingerprint records are excepted, the Criminal Information Center keeps a nonpublic record for first-offender determinations, and an employer may still ask whether an order of expunction was entered.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: First-offender status is uncertain, or the participant has any prior conviction anywhere.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: First-offender status is the whole eligibility test on this track and the platform does not certify it; the matter routes to advice.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant has any prior expunged case.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Under § 99-19-71(3) an earlier expungement does not restore first-offender status.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The offence may be a traffic violation.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Subsection (1) excludes traffic violations and many Mississippi misdemeanours sit near that line; the platform does not classify it.
DUI has its own route and is never handled here.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The conviction is in municipal court and the participant also has justice court convictions.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The matter may be better handled on the additional-misdemeanours track; the packet does not decide it.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant is not a United States citizen.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Immigration consequences are outside the approved self-help boundary.

attachments.conditionDescription: Advisable on every track and effectively necessary wherever first-offender status is in issue; the first-offender statement is initialled only after checking it.

attachments.title: Account balance sheet from the clerk showing a zero balance
attachments.conditionDescription: Advisable everywhere; required in practice in many courts even though subsection (1) does not say so.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court of conviction
attachments.whyNeeded: Courts commonly require a zero balance in practice, and the fines-paid answer is checked against it.

attachments.title: Docket sheet for the case
attachments.conditionDescription: Required in practice on conviction tracks; advisable on every track.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was heard
attachments.whyNeeded: It shows every court-imposed term and whether each was satisfied.

participantChecklist.text: Identify which of Mississippi's four trial court levels entered the conviction and its county or city, and confirm both with that court's records office.
Obtain the certified judgment, the docket sheet, the account balance sheet and your own Mississippi criminal history record, and fill every blank from the records, never from memory.

Initial the first-offender and nontraffic statements only if each is true after checking the criminal history record; any prior conviction, prior expungement, possible traffic classification or DUI is a stop.
Call the records office of the convicting court before filing to confirm the fee, any pauper's-affidavit route, any preferred local form, the copy count and any approved-as-to-form practice.
Confirm the prosecuting authority and its mailing address with the court's records office, serve by mail or hand delivery, and complete the certificate of service only after service occurs.
